text:
Kilmar Ábrego García, the Salvadoran national whose mistaken deportation turned him into a symbol of Donald Trump’s mass deportation efforts, has landed in Spain.
Ábrego García arrived in Madrid on Wednesday after leaving the United States of his own volition. Prior to his departure, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents met him at the airport and removed his ankle monitor, according to We Are CASA, a Maryland-based advocacy group.
The interaction, the group noted, was “a powerful symbol that ends a chapter marked by illegal deportation, imprisonment, abuse at Cecot, retaliatory prosecution, and government surveillance”.
As he made his way through the Madrid airport, Ábrego García did not speak to reporters, instead raising his fist in the air as he climbed into a waiting van.
In a statement provided by We Are CASA, he described his departure from the US as proof that justice was still capable of prevailing over the most powerful government in the world.
“In this case, despite everything they tried to say, every obstacle they put in my way, and every attempt to shame me, justice prevailed under this administration in a way that many people never thought was possible,” he said. “I am leaving happy. I am leaving with my freedom.”
Ábrego García became a lightning rod in the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown in 2025 after he was deported to El Salvador in what an official later called an “administrative error”.
The 31-year-old had been living in the US since 2019, after a judge ruled that he could not be deported to El Salvador due to the dangers posed by a gang that had threatened his family.
Married to an American woman, the Maryland resident was sent to Cecot, a notorious anti-terrorism mega-prison, in violation of the US immigration judge’s 2019 order.
Amid public outcry, he was returned to the US after a decision by the supreme court. Since then, Ábrego García has been fighting government efforts to deport him for a second time to a series of African countries proposed by Department of Homeland Security officials.
On Wednesday, his lawyer, Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg, said that the Trump administration had wanted to deport Ábrego García “handcuffed, on an ICE flight bound for Liberia” on Tuesday.
“And what happened? He walked out a free man, without any restrictions, without shackles on his feet. He left for the country of his choosing, and he did so on a commercial flight, alongside everyone else,” Sandoval-Moshenberg added, describing it as “a victory”.
The Washington Post reported earlier this week that Ábrego García had negotiated a deal with federal authorities to depart the US voluntarily in order to avoid being forcibly removed. The US Department of Homeland Security said Tuesday that Ábrego García had “self-deported” to Spain.
Sandoval-Moshenberg described Ábrego García’s departure from the US as temporary. “Mr Ábrego García has many options to return to the United States as the husband of a US citizen spouse and the father of a US citizen child,” he said. “We don’t expect that to happen under this administration, which we know will never give him a fair shake, but we expect that the next administration will prioritise reunifying this family and bringing him back to Maryland.”
On Wednesday, Ábrego García’s lawyer, Chris Newman, said his client had landed in Spain as a tourist. “I can confirm that he’s coming here with the intention of staying for just a few days and that he already has tickets, one could say, for his next appointment,” he told Spanish media.
His departure this week was celebrated by many who had sought to push back against the Trump administration’s pursuit of Ábrego García. “A year and a half ago, the Trump Admin wanted to leave Kilmar to rot in a Salvadoran gulag,” said Chris Van Hollen, the Maryland senator who visited Abrego Garcia at Cecot, in a statement.
“Today, he is traveling to a country of his choice, a free man – unharmed and with dignity.”
